html:
The tögrög is the currency of Mongolia, first issued in December 1925, four years after the revolution that made Mongolia a Soviet ally. The word means "circle", for a round coin. It replaced a jumble of Chinese silver, Russian roubles, Mexican dollars and even bricks of pressed tea, which had all served as money on the steppe.

The Mongolian Trade and Industry Bank, set up with Soviet help in 1924, issued it, and its value was tied to the Soviet rouble. Early notes carried the Soyombo symbol. Notes of the communist era showed Sükhbaatar, and after 1990 Genghis Khan returned to the larger notes.

After the democratic revolution of 1990, the tögrög was set free to float and lost most of its value in the inflation of the early 1990s. Since then its value has risen and fallen with the prices of copper and coal, Mongolia's main exports.
